root_cause: Arrow key navigation updates aria-selected and activates the tab panel but does not move focus to the newly selected tab, causing focus to be lost after the previous tab is blurred.
repair_strategy: Modify the Tab class's _activate method to focus the tab element after setting aria-selected=true, but only for elements with role='tab', ensuring focus follows selection as required by ARIA tablist patterns.

edits.after:
element.removeAttribute('tabindex')
        element.setAttribute('aria-selected', true)
        element.focus()
        this._toggleDropDown(element, true)
        EventHandler.trigger(element, EVENT_SHOWN, {
          relatedTarget: relatedElem
        })

expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing ArrowRight or ArrowLeft will move focus to the next or previous tab while updating its aria-selected state, providing keyboard operability and conforming to the ARIA Authoring Practices Guide for tablists.
functional_risks: Calling focus() on an already focused element is harmless but may fire redundant focus/blur events.
If a custom implementation relies on the tab receiving focus only after a user click, this change could alter timing of focus-related side effects.
verification_requirements: After ArrowRight press from the Account tab, focus is on the Notifications tab and its aria-selected is true.
After ArrowLeft press from the Notifications tab, focus returns to the Account tab and its aria-selected is true.
Tab panels still show/hide correctly when tabs are activated via arrow keys or mouse clicks.
Initial tab receives focus on page load if it is already active and focusable.
